dedupe_keys.name: usgs global distribution of selected mines deposits and districts of critical minerals pp1802

description: This USGS geodatabase gives point and polygon layers of mines, deposits, districts and mineral regions worldwide for 22 minerals considered critical to the US economy and security in 2017, among them antimony, cobalt, gallium, graphite, lithium, manganese, niobium, platinum-group elements, rare earth elements, tin, titanium, vanadium and zirconium; selenium locations are left out. The ScienceBase page says it accompanies USGS Professional Paper 1802, Critical mineral resources of the United States, which updates Professional Paper 820 from 1973, by Labay, Burger, Bellora, Schulz, DeYoung, Seal, Bradley, Mauk and San Juan. It was published on 19 December 2017 as downloadable zipped shapefiles, a file geodatabase of about 6.5 MB and FGDC metadata, with interactive maps on USGS Mineral Resources Online; USGS data are free and in the public domain (the licence is not stated on the page read). Coverage is global. Caveats: the selection reflects the 2017 critical minerals list and is not updated, and it is not a complete inventory of all mines. For simulation it maps where critical mineral supply sits, for supply chain disruption and hazard exposure scenarios of battery, electronics and energy transition inputs. Related catalogue records include the USGS Mineral Resources Data System, the USMIN mine features and the Canadian critical minerals mines and facilities data.
